# EVE-Cyno Data API

> Deterministic EVE Online data and calculation tools over REST (OpenAPI 3.1) and MCP. No language model is in the loop; the same inputs give the same answers, and every answer names its sources.

Machine-readable description: [/v1/openapi.yaml](/v1/openapi.yaml) (OpenAPI 3.1; JSON at /v1/openapi.json). This file is the same information in prose, generated from the same route table and tool registry.

## Conventions

- Errors are JSON, always: `{"error":{"code":"...","message":"..."}}`. Codes: `not_found`, `method_not_allowed`, `invalid_request`, `payload_too_large`, `rate_limited`, `daily_quota_exceeded`, `unavailable`, `upstream_error`, `upstream_busy`, `unknown_tool`, `tool_disabled`, `api_key_required`, `invalid_api_key`, `key_not_permitted`, `invalid_arguments`, `timeout`, `internal_error`.
- Every response carries `X-Request-ID`: your value when it is a token of 1-64 characters from `[A-Za-z0-9._-]`, otherwise a generated one.
- Requests are rate limited per caller (sliding window): per API key when one is sent, otherwise per client IP. A refused request is `429` with `Retry-After`.
- One call is one request against every limit, however long its list arguments; each list argument has its own cap (see the tool).
- Without an API key the API is for trying it out: 200 requests per UTC day per client (counted per client IP; the documentation routes are not counted) and the lower per-minute limits stated on the operations. Over the day's budget a client gets `429` `daily_quota_exceeded` with `Retry-After` set to the seconds until 00:00 UTC. A free API key is for real use.
- An API key raises the per-minute budgets: every operation states its limit without a key and with one, counted in the key's own window. The live-data tools keep a lower limit than the route.
- A new API key has a daily cap of 10000 requests per UTC day by default (a cap can be changed per key, 0 meaning none). Over its cap a key gets `429` `daily_quota_exceeded` with `Retry-After` set to the seconds until 00:00 UTC.
- Request bodies are capped: 256 KiB on the fit routes, 64 KiB on the tool and MCP endpoints (`413`).
- Tool tiers: each tool is *public* (no key), *keyed* (an API key) or *disabled*. Public: `get_market_price`, `get_type_info`, `search_item_by_name`, `get_ship_stats`, `get_ship_bonuses`, `find_canonical_module`, `get_hull_facts`, `get_fits`, `list_fits`, `validate_fitting`, `compute_fit_stats`, `appraise_items`, `get_production_chain`, `get_jumps_between`, `get_jump_distances`, `plan_jump_route`, `get_systems_in_region`, `get_lp_offers`, `get_npc_stations`, `get_reprocessing_yield`, `get_required_skills`, `get_average_prices`, `get_market_history`, `get_sovereignty`, `get_system_activity`, `find_systems`, `get_system_info`, `get_thera_connections`. Keyed (send the key as `Authorization: Bearer <key>` or `X-API-Key`; `401 api_key_required` without one, `401 invalid_api_key` for a key that is not valid, on every tool): `analyze_battle`. Optional: your own Janice key in the `X-Janice-Key` request header (used for that request only, never logged or stored) turns `appraise_items` into a Janice appraisal; without it the answer is an estimate from ESI average prices. Disabled tools are not offered on this service (`403 tool_disabled` over REST, absent from the MCP tool list).

## Endpoints

### GET /v1/fits/search

Searches the community-fit corpus (EVE Workbench, Abysstracker and other sources named in each hit). The facet parameters filter the corpus; with `q` a filtered vector search ranks the hits. When the facets match nothing they are relaxed one at a time, last first: `relaxed` is then true and `dropped` names what was removed. `ship` may be a loose hull name (`megath` finds Megathron). No language model is involved. Every hit carries an `attribution` object (`source`, `source_url`, `author` when known, `license`, `credit` and `license_url` when the terms require them); show it wherever you show the fit. The fits are community data served ranked and capped, not for bulk export. Free-text search (`q`) needs an API key (`401 api_key_required` without one; `401 invalid_api_key` for a key that is not valid) because it embeds the query; the filters work without a key.

Rate limit: 30 requests per minute per client IP without an API key, 240 per minute per API key with one.

Query parameters:

- `ship`: Hull name; a partial or loose name is resolved against the SDE.
- `activity`: Activity tag, e.g. `pve` or `pvp`.
- `tag`: Extra tag, e.g. `abyss` or `ratting`.
- `filament`: Abyssal filament type.
- `cost`: Cost class tag, e.g. `cheap`.
- `source`: Restrict to one corpus source; empty searches the default source set.
- `clone`: `alpha` keeps only alpha-clone fits, `omega` only omega-only fits; empty keeps both. One of: alpha, omega.
- `q`: Free-text query; empty lists by the facets alone.
- `limit`: Maximum hits, clamped to 1-24 (the response `limit` and `note` say so). There is no offset, page or cursor: one query reaches one ranked page, and a request carrying such a parameter is refused with `invalid_request`.

Response `200`: FitSearchResult with fields `total`, `relaxed`, `dropped`, `hits`, `ship_counts`, `limit`, `note`

### POST /v1/fits/detail

Parses an EFT block and returns its slots, CPU / powergrid / calibration use and ship class. Deterministic; DPS and EHP are not part of this view (see `/fit/stats`).

Rate limit: 60 requests per minute per client IP without an API key, 120 per minute per API key with one.

JSON body:

- `eft` (string, required): The fit as an EFT block (`[Hull, Name]` header, then one module per line).
- `cost` (boolean): Also price the fit when a price source is configured on the server.

Response `200`: FitDetail with fields `ship_name`, `ship_type_id`, `ship_class`, `slots`, `resources`, `drones`, `cost_text`, `eft`, `notes`, `valid`, `unresolved`, `violations`

### POST /v1/fit/stats

Parses an EFT block and returns the Gofa engine's DPS, tank, capacitor, navigation, targeting and drone numbers. Deterministic; the same engine produces the numbers of the `compute_fit_stats` tool.

Rate limit: 60 requests per minute per client IP without an API key, 120 per minute per API key with one.

JSON body:

- `eft` (string, required): The fit as an EFT block.
- `activeDrones` (array of integer): Type IDs of the drones to launch, in priority order; omitted means automatic.

Response `200`: FitStats with fields `DPS`, `Volley`, `Tank`, `Capacitor`, `Navigation`, `Range`, `Targeting`, `Drones`, `Estimated`, `Unmodelled`

### POST /v1/fit/suggest

Ranks the modules that can fill a slot tier of the given fit: how often similar community fits carry them (when the corpus is up), their meta tier, and whether they fit the remaining CPU and powergrid. Without the corpus the ranking falls back to the SDE alone.

Rate limit: 60 requests per minute per client IP without an API key, 120 per minute per API key with one.

JSON body:

- `eft` (string, required): The current fit as an EFT block.
- `slot` (string, required): The slot tier to fill. One of: high, mid, low, rig.

Response `200`: array of Suggestion with fields `typeID`, `name`, `slot`, `metaTier`, `cpu`, `pg`, `fits`, `reason`

### GET /v1/items/search

Name search over the SDE's fittable modules, charges or drones (the fitting palette's search).

Rate limit: 120 requests per minute per client IP without an API key, 240 per minute per API key with one.

Query parameters:

- `q` (required): Name fragment; at least 2 characters.
- `kind`: What to search. One of: module, charge, drone.
- `slot`: For modules: restrict to one slot tier. One of: high, mid, low, rig.
- `limit`: Maximum hits.

Response `200`: array of ModuleHit with fields `typeID`, `name`, `groupID`, `slot`, `metaTier`, `cpu`, `pg`, `canLoadCharge`, `canOverheat`

### POST /v1/tool/{name}

Runs one tool (see Tools). The body is the tool's arguments as a JSON object; the response is `{"tool", "version", "result": {"text", "data"}, "attribution": [{"name", "url", "license"}]}`. `result.text` is the answer as the chat assistant reads it, `result.data` the typed result where the tool has one (otherwise null), `attribution` the upstreams behind the answer.

Rate limit: 10 requests per minute per client IP without an API key, 60 per minute per API key with one.

### POST /v1/mcp

Streamable-HTTP MCP server (stateless, JSON responses): the same tools as `/tool/{name}`, for MCP clients such as Claude Desktop or Claude Code. POST one JSON-RPC 2.0 message per request (`initialize`, `tools/list`, `tools/call`, ...); a notification is answered `202` with no body. `GET` and `DELETE` are not supported in stateless mode (405). Point a client at this URL; it is not meant to be called by hand.

Rate limit: 20 requests per minute per client IP without an API key, 120 per minute per API key with one.

Response `200`: The JSON-RPC 2.0 response.

### GET /v1/health

Always 200 while the process serves; a degraded dependency shows in the body, never in the status. The flags say which dependencies loaded, so a degraded service (no SDE, no fit corpus) can be told from a healthy one. `corpus` is true only when the fit corpus is configured and its backend answered a probe (cached for 30 seconds, 1 second timeout); `corpus_configured` is true when a corpus is wired at all, reachable or not. `sde_build` is the build id of the SDE the service reads, when known.

Response `200`: HealthResponse with fields `status`, `sde`, `corpus`, `corpus_configured`, `stats`, `sde_build`

### GET /v1/openapi.yaml

The OpenAPI 3.1 document of this service, generated from its route table and tool registry.

Rate limit: 60 requests per minute per client IP without an API key, 120 per minute per API key with one.

Response `200`: The OpenAPI document.

### GET /v1/openapi.json

The same OpenAPI 3.1 document as JSON.

Rate limit: 60 requests per minute per client IP without an API key, 120 per minute per API key with one.

Response `200`: The OpenAPI document.

## Tools

Tools are listed public first, then keyed; each says how to authenticate.

The same tools are MCP tools of the same name at `/v1/mcp`; over MCP, `content[0]` is `result.text`, `structuredContent` is `result.data` and `_meta` carries the attribution.

### get_market_price

Get current market prices for an EVE Online item in The Forge region (Jita hub). Returns best sell price, best buy price, and order counts. Set hub (jita, amarr, dodixie, rens, hek) for the orders at that trade hub's main station; without hub the answer covers the whole region of The Forge.

- Call: `POST /v1/tool/get_market_price` or MCP tool `get_market_price`
- Access: public. No key needed.
- Live ESI data: Reads live public data from EVE's ESI through a shared cache that follows ESI's `Expires`. All live-upstream calls share one fair-use limit of 5 calls per minute per caller without an API key and 10 with one (REST and MCP together, counted across every live tool), on top of the route limit. When the shared ESI budget is nearly spent the call is refused with `503 upstream_busy` (MCP: an error result starting `upstream_busy`) and `Retry-After`; retry later.
- Arguments:
  - `type_id` (integer, required): The EVE type ID of the item (e.g. 34 for Tritanium, 44992 for PLEX)
  - `hub` (string): Trade hub whose main station's orders to read, e.g. 'amarr'. Omit for the whole region of The Forge. Ignored for PLEX. One of: jita, amarr, dodixie, rens, hek.
  - `type_name` (string): Human-readable item name, for display only
- Typed result (`result.data`): MarketPrice with fields `type_id`, `region_id`, `market`, `hub`, `best_sell_isk`, `sell_orders`, `best_buy_isk`, `buy_orders`
- Sources: ESI (EVE Swagger Interface)

### get_type_info

Get information about an EVE Online item: name, description, volume, mass, group.

- Call: `POST /v1/tool/get_type_info` or MCP tool `get_type_info`
- Access: public. No key needed.
- Live ESI data: Reads live public data from EVE's ESI through a shared cache that follows ESI's `Expires`. All live-upstream calls share one fair-use limit of 5 calls per minute per caller without an API key and 10 with one (REST and MCP together, counted across every live tool), on top of the route limit. When the shared ESI budget is nearly spent the call is refused with `503 upstream_busy` (MCP: an error result starting `upstream_busy`) and `Retry-After`; retry later.
- Arguments:
  - `type_id` (integer, required): The EVE type ID
- Typed result (`result.data`): TypeInfo with fields `type_id`, `name`, `description`, `volume_m3`, `mass_kg`, `group_id`, `meta_group`, `meta_level`, `tech_level`, `market_group_path`, `base_price`, `portion_size`, `packaged_volume_m3`, `capacity_m3`
- Sources: EVE Static Data Export (via Fuzzwork); ESI (EVE Swagger Interface)

### search_item_by_name

Resolve one or more EVE Online item, ship, or module names to their type_id. Call this BEFORE get_market_price or get_type_info when you only have a name, not a type_id.

- Call: `POST /v1/tool/search_item_by_name` or MCP tool `search_item_by_name`
- Access: public. No key needed.
- Arguments:
  - `names` (array of string, required): List of item/ship/module names to resolve, e.g. ['Stabber', 'PLEX', 'Gila']
  - `details` (boolean): true: one line of facts per item (group, category, meta group and level, market group, volume, Alpha usability and, for Abyssal Deadspace NPCs and filaments, their combat profile or tier and weather) for up to 50 names; use it to classify a list ('which of these are Tech II or faction')
- Typed result (`result.data`): ItemList with fields `items`, `unresolved`
- Sources: EVE Static Data Export (via Fuzzwork)

### get_ship_stats

Get slot layout, hardpoints, and resource limits for an EVE Online ship. Call this BEFORE generating a fit to know exact hi/mid/low/rig slot counts, turret and launcher hardpoints, CPU capacity (tf), and powergrid capacity (MW). Using these values prevents generating fits that exceed slot or resource limits.

- Call: `POST /v1/tool/get_ship_stats` or MCP tool `get_ship_stats`
- Access: public. No key needed.
- Arguments:
  - `ship_name` (string, required): The ship type name, e.g. 'Vexor', 'Rifter', 'Stabber', 'Gila'
- Typed result (`result.data`): ShipStats with fields `type_id`, `name`, `attributes`
- Sources: EVE Static Data Export (via Fuzzwork)

### get_ship_bonuses

Get hull bonuses for an EVE Online ship — per-skill-level bonuses + role bonuses + ship class. Call this BEFORE generating a fit so you pick the bonused weapon system (Caldari hybrid vs missile, Gallente drone vs hybrid, Minmatar projectile vs missile, Amarr laser; pirate hulls have specific role bonuses like web range or ECM). The response names every per-skill bonus and any role bonus from the ship's ESI description — use those to decide weapons, modules, and tank type.

- Call: `POST /v1/tool/get_ship_bonuses` or MCP tool `get_ship_bonuses`
- Access: public. No key needed.
- Arguments:
  - `ship_name` (string, required): Ship type name, e.g. 'Hawk', 'Stabber Fleet Issue', 'Daredevil', 'Gila'
- Typed result: none; the answer is `result.text`
- Sources: EVE Static Data Export (via Fuzzwork); EVE Workbench

### find_canonical_module

Look up canonical SDE typeNames for a module family (e.g. 'Steel Plates', 'Entropic Radiation Sink', 'Shield Extender', 'Heat Sink', 'Magnetic Field Stabilizer', 'Ballistic Control System', 'Stasis Webifier', 'Microwarpdrive', 'Remote Armor Repairer'). Call this when you are about to write a module that isn't in the `compatible_weapons` or `bonused_modules` of get_hull_facts and you are not 100% sure of the canonical name. Optional `size` narrows to a class prefix — 'Small' for frigates / destroyers, 'Medium' for cruisers / battlecruisers, 'Large' for battleships and capitals. Returns a short list of real published items (no SKINs / Blueprints / Specializations). Search mode (when slot, kind, meta or limit is set): list modules, charges or drones by slot, kind and meta group, e.g. family 'Shield' + slot 'mid', in name order with CPU and powergrid, up to 30 per call with the total. Example: {"family":"Shield Extender","slot":"mid","meta":"Tech II"}.

- Call: `POST /v1/tool/find_canonical_module` or MCP tool `find_canonical_module`
- Access: public. No key needed.
- Arguments:
  - `family` (string, required): Module family substring, e.g. 'Steel Plates', 'Entropic Radiation Sink', 'Tracking Enhancer'
  - `kind` (string): Search mode: what to list (default module). Charges and drones have no slot. One of: module, charge, drone.
  - `limit` (integer): Search mode: items to list (1-30, default 10)
  - `meta` (string): Search mode: meta group name, e.g. 'Tech II', 'Faction', 'Deadspace', 'Officer', 'Abyssal'
  - `size` (string): Optional size class — 'Small', 'Medium', or 'Large'
  - `slot` (string): Search mode: only modules that fit this slot, e.g. 'mid'. One of: high, mid, low, rig.
- Typed result (`result.data`): ModuleList with fields `total`, `shown`, `modules`
- Sources: EVE Static Data Export (via Fuzzwork)

### get_hull_facts

Authoritative SDE snapshot of a hull's fitting envelope — slot/hardpoint counts, drone bay, role/skill bonuses, AND the canonical list of weapons that hull is restricted to fit (when EVE encodes a per-hull weapon lock). Call this BEFORE writing an EFT block on any unfamiliar / specialist hull (Triglavian battleships Leshak / Drekavac → Supratidal Entropic Disintegrators; Triglavian frigates → Light variants; Triglavian cruisers → Heavy variants; pirate / faction hulls). When `compatible_weapons` is non-empty, USE ONLY those typeNames — anything else will be rejected by validate_fitting. When `compatible_weapons` is empty there is no per-hull lock; rely on `role_bonuses` (which carry the bonused weapon family like 'Small Hybrid Turret' or 'Light Missile') and standard hardpoint sizing.

- Call: `POST /v1/tool/get_hull_facts` or MCP tool `get_hull_facts`
- Access: public. No key needed.
- Arguments:
  - `ship_name` (string, required): Ship type name, e.g. 'Leshak', 'Hecate', 'Vedmak', 'Damavik'
- Typed result: none; the answer is `result.text`
- Sources: EVE Static Data Export (via Fuzzwork); EVE Workbench

### get_fits

Retrieve community ship fits from the indexed fit database, with author and source link for each. Returns the raw EFT text (header + modules + drones + ammo) and the source URL for each match. Filter by ship_name (exact), activity (pvp / pve / hauler / exploration / mining / logistics), context (wh, abyss, abyss-electrical / firestorm / exotic / gamma / dark, abyss-t1..t6, ratting, solo), cost_class (cheap < 50M / mid 50-500M / blingy > 500M ISK), alpha_clone (true for Alpha-skill-friendly), combat_role (solo / fleet — zKillboard only), source (workbench / abysstracker / gustavmannfred / caldarijoans: restrict to one source), limit (default 5, at most 10), fit_id (fetch one fit by the id that list_fits and get_fits print; the other filters are ignored), include_eft (false leaves the EFT blocks out and lists the ids only). If nothing matches, the answer says 'NO FITS FOUND'; dropping the most restrictive filter may find some.

- Call: `POST /v1/tool/get_fits` or MCP tool `get_fits`
- Access: public. No key needed.
- Arguments:
  - `activity` (string): Activity the fit is meant for. One of: pvp, pve, hauler, exploration, mining, logistics.
  - `alpha_clone` (boolean): If true, only return fits flyable on Alpha skills.
  - `combat_role` (string): Workbench-derived role tag for PvP fits. One of: solo, fleet.
  - `context` (string): Subcontext tag. Examples: 'wh' (wormhole), 'abyss' (any abyss), 'abyss-electrical', 'abyss-firestorm', 'abyss-exotic', 'abyss-gamma', 'abyss-dark', 'abyss-t1', 'abyss-t2', 'abyss-t3', 'abyss-t4', 'abyss-t5', 'abyss-t6', 'ratting', 'solo'.
  - `cost_class` (string): cheap (< 50M ISK), mid (50-500M), blingy (> 500M). One of: cheap, mid, blingy.
  - `fit_id` (string): Fetch one fit by its id: the UUID printed as id= on a fit's meta line (always in the public API text; in chat text only when include_eft is false) or the fit_id field of the result data. The other filters are ignored. Example: '6f1d3b2a-0c4e-5a7b-9d8e-1f2a3b4c5d6e'.
  - `include_eft` (boolean): Default true. false leaves the EFT blocks out and lists only the meta line and id of each fit, to browse cheaply before fetching one with fit_id.
  - `limit` (integer): Max number of fits to return (default 5, hard max 10).
  - `ship_name` (string): Exact EVE ship name. Examples: 'Tengu', 'Gila', 'Hurricane Fleet Issue', 'Vexor Navy Issue'. Leave empty to search across all ships matching the other filters.
  - `source` (string): Restrict to one source. Leave empty to search all sources. Use 'gustavmannfred' for Gustav's abyss fits (gustavmannfred.streamlit.app), 'caldarijoans' for CaldariJoans' abyss fits (caldarijoans.streamlit.app). Pass this when the user explicitly asks for a specific author's fit. One of: workbench, abysstracker, gustavmannfred, caldarijoans.
- Typed result (`result.data`): CommunityFits with fields `found`, `relaxed`, `fits`
- Sources: EVE Workbench; Abysstracker; gustavmannfred (abyss fits); caldarijoans (abyss fits); zKillboard

### list_fits

LIST / enumerate community fits from the indexed fit database by exact payload filters (NOT semantic search). Use when the user wants to SEE WHAT FITS EXIST — 'list all fits for X', 'what Gila fits do you have', 'how many workbench fits', 'show every abyss-t5 fit' — rather than one fit to copy. Returns a compact numbered list (ship — fit name | tags | source URL) plus the TOTAL match count. Filter by source, ship_name (exact), tag (a fit_tags value like 'pve' / 'pvp' / 'abyss-t5' / 'cheap' / 'alpha-clone'), and filament_type. Use get_fits instead when the user wants the actual modules to copy.

- Call: `POST /v1/tool/list_fits` or MCP tool `list_fits`
- Access: public. No key needed.
- Arguments:
  - `filament_type` (string): Abysstracker filament: electrical / firestorm / exotic / gamma / dark.
  - `limit` (integer): Max rows to list (default 24, hard max 24: the list is capped, not exportable).
  - `ship_name` (string): Exact EVE ship name to filter by (e.g. 'Gila'). Empty = all ships.
  - `source` (string): Restrict to one fit source. Empty = all fit sources. One of: workbench, abysstracker, zkillboard_meta, gustavmannfred, caldarijoans.
  - `tag` (string): A fit_tags value to filter by: pvp / pve / abyss / abyss-t1..t6 / wh / cheap / blingy / alpha-clone / solo / fleet, etc.
- Typed result (`result.data`): FitListing with fields `total`, `shown`, `fits`
- Sources: EVE Workbench; Abysstracker; gustavmannfred (abyss fits); caldarijoans (abyss fits); zKillboard

### analyze_battle

Analyze a battle report from zKillboard, WarBeacon, or br.evetools.org. Call this when the user pastes a zKillboard URL containing '/related/' or '/br/', a WarBeacon URL containing '/br/report/', or a br.evetools.org URL containing '/br/{24-hex-id}'. Returns kills, ISK destroyed, ship composition, and duration. Pass detail='full' to additionally include a per-weapon damage breakdown and a per-slot list of destroyed modules — use this on the user's follow-up when they ask for damage / weapons / modules / components / what killed.

- Call: `POST /v1/tool/analyze_battle` or MCP tool `analyze_battle`
- Access: keyed. Send an API key as `Authorization: Bearer <key>` or `X-API-Key: <key>`; `401 api_key_required` without one, `401 invalid_api_key` for an invalid one.
- Arguments:
  - `battle_url` (string, required): Full battle URL. Supported formats: https://zkillboard.com/related/30003067/202501071700/ or https://zkillboard.com/br/4885/ or https://warbeacon.net/br/report/78f57bba-34b0-4e0b-b0e6-53119ab32fbc or https://br.evetools.org/br/69f7d88dcbe9de00126eb5a5
  - `detail` (string): Output level. 'summary' (default) — high-level battle report only. 'full' — also includes top-10 damage by weapon type per side and top-10 destroyed modules per slot per side. Slower (~5-15 s) since it fetches individual killmails; for br.evetools.org reports only the 25 most valuable are read, one at a time. The result is cached for 30 min so a follow-up turn is fast. One of: summary, full.
- Typed result: none; the answer is `result.text`
- Sources: zKillboard; WarBeacon; br.evetools.org; ESI (EVE Swagger Interface); EVE Static Data Export (via Fuzzwork)

### validate_fitting

Validate an EVE Online ship fitting in EFT format. Checks CPU, powergrid, and slot counts against ship attributes assuming Engineering V (+25% PG) and Electronics V (+25% CPU) — the realistic baseline every PvP / abyss capable character has. Call this after generating a fit to confirm it is valid before presenting it to the user.

- Call: `POST /v1/tool/validate_fitting` or MCP tool `validate_fitting`
- Access: public. No key needed.
- Arguments:
  - `eft_text` (string, required): Full fitting in EFT format, starting with [Ship Name, Fit Name]
- Typed result (`result.data`): FitValidation with fields `ship`, `valid`, `cpu`, `pg`, `slots`, `violations`, `warnings`, `unresolved_modules`, `data_source`, `alpha_unchecked`, `stats`
- Sources: EVE Static Data Export (via Fuzzwork); ESI (EVE Swagger Interface)

### compute_fit_stats

Compute the real stats of an EVE Online fit from its EFT text with the dogma engine (all-V skills, no implants): DPS per weapon group with the charge used, volley, EHP per layer with resists, max speed (propulsion on), align time, capacitor stability and CPU/PG load. Call this whenever the user asks for a fit's DPS, EHP, tank, speed, align or cap stability - never estimate these by hand. Weapons with no charge on their EFT line get a default T1 ammo (Scourge missiles; Phased Plasma / Antimatter / Multifrequency for turrets), which the output labels.

- Call: `POST /v1/tool/compute_fit_stats` or MCP tool `compute_fit_stats`
- Access: public. No key needed.
- Arguments:
  - `eft_text` (string, required): Full fitting in EFT format, starting with [Ship Name, Fit Name]. Loaded ammo may be given as 'Module, Charge' lines.
  - `charges` (object): Optional ammo to use instead of the default, as {module name: charge name}, e.g. {"Rocket Launcher II": "Mjolnir Rocket"}. Only for weapons with no charge on their EFT line.
- Typed result (`result.data`): FitStatCard with fields `hull`, `basis`, `dps`, `weapon_dps`, `drone_dps`, `volley`, `weapons`, `drones`, `tank`, `speed_ms`, `prop_on`, `align_s`, `signature_m`, `cap`, `load`, `no_ammo`, `unresolved_charges`, `unresolved_modules`
- Sources: EVE Static Data Export (via Fuzzwork)

### appraise_items

Appraise a list of EVE Online items and return the total ISK value. Without a Janice key the answer is an estimate from EVE's average prices (ESI /markets/prices, refreshed daily), not live Jita buy or sell prices. With a Janice key it is a Janice appraisal: Jita buy, sell and split totals and a link to the full appraisal. The answer names its price source: pass it on, and call an estimate an estimate.

- Call: `POST /v1/tool/appraise_items` or MCP tool `appraise_items`
- Access: public. No key needed.
- Optional: your own Janice API key in the `X-Janice-Key` header (REST and MCP over HTTP) makes it a Janice appraisal instead of the ESI estimate; it is used for that request only and never logged or stored.
- Arguments:
  - `items` (string, required): Items one per line with a quantity: multi-buy ('Tritanium x1000' or 'Tritanium 1000'), an inventory or contract copy, or an EFT fit
- Typed result: none; the answer is `result.text`
- Sources: ESI (EVE Swagger Interface); EVE Static Data Export (via Fuzzwork); Janice

### get_production_chain

Compute the full material breakdown to manufacture an EVE Online item, recursively expanding sub-components down to base minerals and PI commodities. Use this for 'how many minerals to build X' or 'production chain for X' questions. Optional advanced params let the user model a specific structure rig + system cost index (e.g., 'in 1DQ1-A with Minmatar manufacturing rig 4 and 5% cost index'). With system it reads that system's live manufacturing cost index from ESI and prices the job fee in ISK; with include_cost it adds the ISK value of the materials at ESI average prices and a total. Planetary commodities (P1-P4) answer with their schematic chain down to P0 raw resources: runs counts cycles of the final schematic, ME, rigs and cost indices do not apply (system is accepted, reads nothing, and still counts as a live call), and include_cost values the raw resources. Without system or include_cost it is SDE-only.

- Call: `POST /v1/tool/get_production_chain` or MCP tool `get_production_chain`
- Access: public. No key needed.
- Live ESI data: Calls with `system` read live public data from EVE's ESI through a shared cache that follows ESI's `Expires`; only those calls count against the fair-use limit below. All live-upstream calls share one fair-use limit of 5 calls per minute per caller without an API key and 10 with one (REST and MCP together, counted across every live tool), on top of the route limit. When the shared ESI budget is nearly spent the call is refused with `503 upstream_busy` (MCP: an error result starting `upstream_busy`) and `Retry-After`; retry later.
- Arguments:
  - `item_name` (string, required): Item or ship name to build, e.g. 'Revelation', 'Avatar', 'Rifter'
  - `facility_tax_pct` (number): Facility tax of the structure in percent, 0 to 10 (default 0.25, an NPC station). Used for the job fee.
  - `include_cost` (boolean): true adds the ISK value of the materials at ESI daily average prices and, with system or system_cost_index, the job fee and a total. Default false.
  - `industry_skills` (object): Optional industry skills dict. Currently honoured: 'production_efficiency' (0-5) for legacy ME-savings adjustment. Modern EVE folded most industry skills into ME research; this is the remaining axis worth modelling explicitly.
  - `me_level` (integer): Material Efficiency level 0-10 (default 10 — fully researched BPO)
  - `runs` (integer): Number of runs (default 1)
  - `station_rig_level` (integer): Structure rig material-savings level 0-5 (default 0). M-Set Manufacturing Material Efficiency rig at level 5 = 10% material savings. Use only when the user explicitly mentions a structure or its rigs.
  - `system` (string): Solar system where the job runs, e.g. 'Jita'. Reads its current manufacturing cost index from ESI and prices the job fee in ISK (live: counts against the live limit). Give this or system_cost_index, not both.
  - `system_cost_index` (number): System manufacturing cost index as a fraction, 0.0-1.0 (real indices stay below about 0.20; default 0.0). Adds a job fee note: job cost = estimated item value × (cost index + facility tax + 4% SCC surcharge), where the estimated item value is the ME 0 inputs at ESI adjusted prices and an NPC station charges 0.25% facility tax; a player structure sets its own facility tax and its bonuses lower the cost index part, and each sub-component job pays its own fee. Set to the user's quoted system index when they ask for a fee estimate, or give system to read it.
- Typed result (`result.data`): ProductionChain with fields `item`, `type_id`, `kind`, `runs`, `me_level`, `materials`, `steps`, `cost`
- Sources: EVE Static Data Export (via Fuzzwork); ESI (EVE Swagger Interface)

### get_jumps_between

Compute the number of jumps and the route between two EVE solar systems. Default route is shortest (any security). Set prefer_high_sec=true to prefer highsec-only paths (longer but safer). Set detail='summary' for one line (jump count, lowest-security hop, highsec/lowsec/nullsec counts and the highsec-only alternative) instead of the hop list. avoid: systems never to route through (up to 20); via: systems to pass through in order (up to 5).

- Call: `POST /v1/tool/get_jumps_between` or MCP tool `get_jumps_between`
- Access: public. No key needed.
- Arguments:
  - `from_system` (string, required): Origin solar system name, e.g. 'Jita'
  - `to_system` (string, required): Destination solar system name, e.g. 'Amarr'
  - `avoid` (array of string): Systems never to route through (up to 20), e.g. ['Ahbazon']. The origin and destination are never avoided.
  - `detail` (string): 'route' (default) lists every hop; 'summary' answers in one line. One of: route, summary.
  - `prefer_high_sec` (boolean): If true, route via highsec only (default false)
  - `via` (array of string): Systems to pass through, in order (up to 5), e.g. ['Dodixie']
- Typed result (`result.data`): Route with fields `from`, `to`, `prefer_high_sec`, `highsec_satisfied`, `jumps`, `systems`, `hops_omitted`, `detail`, `via`, `avoid`, `lowest_security_hop`, `counts_by_class`, `highsec_only_jumps`
- Sources: EVE Static Data Export (via Fuzzwork)

### get_jump_distances

Jump counts from one origin system to up to 200 other systems in one call (one search over the stargate graph). Use it to rank candidates by distance, e.g. 'which of these systems is nearest to C-N4OD'. One line per system, nearest first; unknown names and systems without a gate route (wormhole space) are listed separately. prefer_high_sec counts highsec-only routes where one exists.

- Call: `POST /v1/tool/get_jump_distances` or MCP tool `get_jump_distances`
- Access: public. No key needed.
- Arguments:
  - `origin` (string, required): Origin solar system name, e.g. 'C-N4OD'
  - `systems` (array of string, required): Solar system names to measure, e.g. ['Elonaya','Uchomida','Actee']
  - `avoid` (array of string): Systems never to pass through (up to 20), e.g. ['Ahbazon']; a target you also list here still gets its own count, but no route passes through it.
  - `prefer_high_sec` (boolean): If true, count highsec-only routes where one exists (default false)
- Typed result (`result.data`): JumpDistances with fields `origin`, `origin_id`, `prefer_high_sec`, `avoid`, `distances`, `unreachable`, `unresolved`
- Sources: EVE Static Data Export (via Fuzzwork)

### plan_jump_route

Plan a jump-drive route like a capital pilot's jump planner, for a jump freighter, Rorqual, Black Ops, carrier, dreadnought, Lancer, FAX, supercarrier or titan (give the hull name), or 'Jump Bridge' for a chain of Ansiblex jump bridges (5 ly): the fewest jumps from origin to destination through optional waypoints, then the fewest light-years. Every hop ends where a cynosural field can be lit (lowsec or nullsec; never highsec, wormhole space, Pochven or Zarzakh); capitals cannot start in highsec. One line per hop: region, system, security, NPC stations, light-years, the gate jumps between the same two systems and the isotopes burned; then the totals (light-years, fuel and its m³). Skills default to level 5. Titans, Black Ops and the Rorqual can also bridge, and carriers, supercarriers, Black Ops and the Rorqual can conduit jump, over the same hops; that fuel is not counted. Example: {"origin":"Amamake","destination":"1DQ1-A","ship":"Rhea"}. avoid_incursions and live_info read live ESI data and count against the live-data limit; without them the route comes from the SDE alone.

- Call: `POST /v1/tool/plan_jump_route` or MCP tool `plan_jump_route`
- Access: public. No key needed.
- Live ESI data: Calls with `avoid_incursions` or `live_info` read live public data from EVE's ESI through a shared cache that follows ESI's `Expires`; only those calls count against the fair-use limit below. All live-upstream calls share one fair-use limit of 5 calls per minute per caller without an API key and 10 with one (REST and MCP together, counted across every live tool), on top of the route limit. When the shared ESI budget is nearly spent the call is refused with `503 upstream_busy` (MCP: an error result starting `upstream_busy`) and `Retry-After`; retry later.
- Arguments:
  - `origin` (string, required): Start solar system name, e.g. 'Amamake'
  - `destination` (string, required): Last stop, a solar system name, e.g. '1DQ1-A'
  - `ship` (string, required): Hull name, e.g. 'Rhea', 'Rorqual', 'Avatar', 'Panther', or 'Jump Bridge' for Ansiblex jump bridges
  - `avoid` (array of string): Systems no hop may end in (up to 20), e.g. ['Tegheon']
  - `avoid_incursions` (boolean): Read the active incursions from ESI (live) and never end a hop in an infested system; incursions jam cynosural fields. Costs one live call.
  - `avoid_regions` (array of string): Regions no hop may end in (up to 10), e.g. ["Khanid"]
  - `live_info` (boolean): Add each hop system's sovereignty holder and last-hour jumps and kills from ESI (live). Costs one live call.
  - `prefer_stations` (boolean): If true, among the routes with the fewest jumps prefer hops that end in systems with an NPC station (default false)
  - `skills` (object): Skill levels 0-5 (default 5 each), e.g. {"jump_drive_calibration": 4}. Jump freighters also use jump_freighters.
  - `waypoints` (array of string): Systems the route must stop at, in order (up to 5), e.g. ["Sahda"]
- Typed result (`result.data`): JumpRoute with fields `origin`, `origin_id`, `destination`, `destination_id`, `waypoints`, `ship`, `ship_group`, `skills`, `range_ly`, `fuel_type`, `fuel_per_ly`, `jumps`, `total_ly`, `total_fuel`, `fuel_volume_m3`, `can_bridge`, `can_conduit`, `prefer_stations`, `avoid`, `avoid_regions`, `avoid_incursions`, `incursion_systems`, `live_info`, `live_unavailable`, `hops`
- Sources: EVE Static Data Export (via Fuzzwork); ESI (EVE Swagger Interface)

### get_systems_in_region

List solar systems in an EVE region filtered by security band. Use for 'which lowsec systems in X' or 'highsec in Y' questions.

- Call: `POST /v1/tool/get_systems_in_region` or MCP tool `get_systems_in_region`
- Access: public. No key needed.
- Arguments:
  - `region_name` (string, required): Region name, e.g. 'Black Rise', 'The Forge'
  - `sec_max` (number): Maximum security (default 1.0)
  - `sec_min` (number): Minimum security (default -1.0)
- Typed result: none; the answer is `result.text`
- Sources: EVE Static Data Export (via Fuzzwork)

### get_lp_offers

List the loyalty point (LP) store of an NPC corporation and rank its offers by the ISK each loyalty point is worth. ISK per LP = (average price of the items given - the ISK cost - the average price of the required items) / the LP cost. The prices are ESI's daily average prices, not live market orders, so treat the figures as a guide; an offer with an item that has no average price (a blueprint copy has none) shows no ISK per LP and says why. A corporation without a store says so. Example: {"corporation":"Caldari Navy","limit":5}. Another: Sisters of EVE offers matching 'probe', cheapest in LP first: {"corporation":"Sisters of EVE","item":"probe","sort":"lp_cost"}.

- Call: `POST /v1/tool/get_lp_offers` or MCP tool `get_lp_offers`
- Access: public. No key needed.
- Live ESI data: Reads live public data from EVE's ESI through a shared cache that follows ESI's `Expires`. All live-upstream calls share one fair-use limit of 5 calls per minute per caller without an API key and 10 with one (REST and MCP together, counted across every live tool), on top of the route limit. When the shared ESI budget is nearly spent the call is refused with `503 upstream_busy` (MCP: an error result starting `upstream_busy`) and `Retry-After`; retry later.
- Arguments:
  - `corporation` (string, required): NPC corporation name, e.g. 'Caldari Navy', 'Sisters of EVE', 'Federation Navy'
  - `item` (string): Keep offers whose item name contains this text, e.g. 'shield'
  - `limit` (integer): Offers to list (1-50, default 20)
  - `sort` (string): Order of the offers: isk_per_lp (default, best first, offers without a value last), lp_cost (cheapest first) or name. One of: isk_per_lp, lp_cost, name.
- Typed result (`result.data`): LPOffers with fields `corporation`, `corporation_id`, `prices_as_of`, `total`, `shown`, `offers`
- Sources: ESI (EVE Swagger Interface); EVE Static Data Export (via Fuzzwork)

### get_npc_stations

List NPC stations, and find mission agents (for example the nearest level 4 security agent). With only system_name it lists that system's stations with owner and operation: use it for 'stations in X' or 'where can I dock'. With near, region, services, agent or limit it searches stations, nearest first (by gate jumps from near.origin), with owner, services, the refinery yield (Reprocessing Plant stations) and the matching agents, up to 50 per call with the total. Every agent in this build sits at a station, so 'nearest level 4 security agent to Dodixie' is the nearest station with such an agent. Example: {"near":{"origin":"Dodixie","max_jumps":5},"agent":{"level":4,"division":"security"},"limit":3}. Another: stations within 1 jump of Dodixie with repair facilities: {"near":{"origin":"Dodixie","max_jumps":1},"services":["Repair Facilities"]}.

- Call: `POST /v1/tool/get_npc_stations` or MCP tool `get_npc_stations`
- Access: public. No key needed.
- Arguments:
  - `agent` (object): Keep stations with at least one matching agent, and list those agents, e.g. {"level":4,"division":"security"} or {"kind":"research","faction":"Gallente Federation"}.
  - `limit` (integer): Stations to list (1-50, default 20)
  - `near` (object): Rank stations by gate jumps from an origin system, nearest first, e.g. {"origin":"Dodixie","max_jumps":5}. Without max_jumps every reachable system is ranked.
  - `region` (string): Region name, e.g. 'Sinq Laison'
  - `services` (array of string): Station services a station must all offer, e.g. ['Repair Facilities', 'Reprocessing Plant']. Same names as find_systems station_services.
  - `system_name` (string): Solar system name, e.g. 'Hek', 'Jita'. Alone it lists that system's stations; with search parameters it limits the search to that system.
- Typed result (`result.data`): StationList with fields `total`, `shown`, `stations`
- Sources: EVE Static Data Export (via Fuzzwork)

### get_reprocessing_yield

Compute the materials produced by reprocessing an EVE item (ore, ice, salvage, modules). Use for 'how many minerals from X Veldspar' or 'reprocessing yield' questions.

- Call: `POST /v1/tool/get_reprocessing_yield` or MCP tool `get_reprocessing_yield`
- Access: public. No key needed.
- Arguments:
  - `item_name` (string, required): Item name, e.g. 'Veldspar', 'Mexallon'
  - `quantity` (integer): Number of units to reprocess (default: one batch, e.g. 100 for most ores)
  - `refining_efficiency_pct` (number): Combined skill+facility yield 0-100 (default 50)
- Typed result: none; the answer is `result.text`
- Sources: EVE Static Data Export (via Fuzzwork)

### get_required_skills

List the skills required to fly a ship or build an item, for one item (item_name) or up to 20 at once (items). Use for 'what skills to fly X' or 'what skills to build Y' questions. With training_time it adds the skill points and the training time from zero SP for an Omega clone; without attributes each skill is at its best remap (27/21). Several items also get the union of their skills, each at its highest level.

- Call: `POST /v1/tool/get_required_skills` or MCP tool `get_required_skills`
- Access: public. No key needed.
- Arguments:
  - `attributes` (object): The character's five attributes, all or none, e.g. {'perception': 20, 'memory': 20, 'willpower': 20, 'intelligence': 20, 'charisma': 19}; each skill then trains by its own two attributes. Only used with training_time.
  - `item_name` (string): Ship or blueprint name, e.g. 'Avatar', 'Nyx', 'Revelation', 'Damage Control II'
  - `items` (array of string): Up to 20 item names for a plan with one line each, e.g. ['Paladin', 'Rifter']; item_name given beside it is added to the list
  - `purpose` (string): 'fly' for ship/module skills (default), 'build' for blueprint manufacturing skills. One of: fly, build.
  - `training_time` (boolean): true: add SP and the training time from zero SP for an Omega clone, e.g. for 'how long to train into a Paladin'. Without attributes each skill is trained at its best remap (primary 27 / secondary 21, no implants, 37.5 SP/min).
- Typed result (`result.data`): SkillPlan with fields `purpose`, `attributes`, `items`, `combined`, `unresolved`
- Sources: EVE Static Data Export (via Fuzzwork)

### get_average_prices

EVE's average price for up to 200 items in one call, by name (names) or type ID (type_ids), from ESI /markets/prices (refreshed daily, one shared copy). It is an average of recent trades across New Eden, not live Jita buy or sell orders: say so when you quote it. Use get_market_price for the live order book of one item.

- Call: `POST /v1/tool/get_average_prices` or MCP tool `get_average_prices`
- Access: public. No key needed.
- Arguments:
  - `names` (array of string): Exact item names, e.g. ['Tritanium', 'PLEX', 'Gila']; up to 200 together with type_ids
  - `type_ids` (array of integer): Item type IDs, e.g. [34, 44992]; up to 200 together with names
- Typed result (`result.data`): AveragePrices with fields `as_of`, `source`, `prices`, `unresolved`
- Sources: ESI (EVE Swagger Interface); EVE Static Data Export (via Fuzzwork)

### get_market_history

Daily market history of one item in one region from ESI (/markets/{region_id}/history), summarised: average, low, high and volume per day or per week over the last 1-90 days, and the change from the first to the last bucket. Name the item (item_name) or give type_id; pick a hub (jita, amarr, dodixie, rens, hek) or a region name (default The Forge). Use for 'is X trending up' or 'how much X trades per day'.

- Call: `POST /v1/tool/get_market_history` or MCP tool `get_market_history`
- Access: public. No key needed.
- Live ESI data: Reads live public data from EVE's ESI through a shared cache that follows ESI's `Expires`. All live-upstream calls share one fair-use limit of 5 calls per minute per caller without an API key and 10 with one (REST and MCP together, counted across every live tool), on top of the route limit. When the shared ESI budget is nearly spent the call is refused with `503 upstream_busy` (MCP: an error result starting `upstream_busy`) and `Retry-After`; retry later.
- Arguments:
  - `bucket` (string): Size of one row: 'week' (ISO weeks, Monday to Sunday; default) or 'day'. One of: day, week.
  - `days` (integer): Length of the window in days, 1 to 90 (default 30), ending at the newest day ESI has
  - `hub` (string): Trade hub whose region to read, e.g. 'amarr'. Wins over region. Omit for The Forge. One of: jita, amarr, dodixie, rens, hek.
  - `item_name` (string): Exact item name, e.g. 'PLEX' or 'Tritanium'. Use this or type_id.
  - `region` (string): Region name, e.g. 'Domain' or 'Sinq Laison'. Default The Forge. PLEX always uses the global PLEX market.
  - `type_id` (integer): The EVE type ID of the item (e.g. 34 for Tritanium). Use this or item_name.
- Typed result (`result.data`): MarketHistory with fields `type_id`, `name`, `region_id`, `region`, `hub`, `days`, `window_end`, `bucket`, `buckets`, `summary`
- Sources: ESI (EVE Swagger Interface); EVE Static Data Export (via Fuzzwork)

### get_sovereignty

Get who holds sovereignty (alliance and corporation, or NPC faction) over EVE solar systems. Live data from ESI. Pass systems (up to 50 names) for one line per system with the holders' names; system_name (one system) is the older form and answers with ids only. Use for 'who controls X' or 'sov holder of Y' questions.

- Call: `POST /v1/tool/get_sovereignty` or MCP tool `get_sovereignty`
- Access: public. No key needed.
- Live ESI data: Reads live public data from EVE's ESI through a shared cache that follows ESI's `Expires`. All live-upstream calls share one fair-use limit of 5 calls per minute per caller without an API key and 10 with one (REST and MCP together, counted across every live tool), on top of the route limit. When the shared ESI budget is nearly spent the call is refused with `503 upstream_busy` (MCP: an error result starting `upstream_busy`) and `Retry-After`; retry later.
- Arguments:
  - `system_name` (string): Solar system name, e.g. 'Saranen' (single system; the older form, answers ids only)
  - `systems` (array of string): Up to 50 solar system names, e.g. ['1DQ1-A', 'Jita']: one line each, with the alliance and corporation names or the NPC faction
- Typed result (`result.data`): SovereigntyList with fields `systems`, `unresolved`, `names_unavailable`
- Sources: EVE Static Data Export (via Fuzzwork); ESI (EVE Swagger Interface)

### get_system_activity

Get the activity of EVE solar systems in the last hour from ESI. Pass systems (up to 50 names) for one line per system with jumps, ship kills, pod kills and NPC kills; system_name (one system) is the older form and answers kills only. Use for 'how busy is X', 'how many kills in Y recently', 'is it safe to undock'.

- Call: `POST /v1/tool/get_system_activity` or MCP tool `get_system_activity`
- Access: public. No key needed.
- Live ESI data: Reads live public data from EVE's ESI through a shared cache that follows ESI's `Expires`. All live-upstream calls share one fair-use limit of 5 calls per minute per caller without an API key and 10 with one (REST and MCP together, counted across every live tool), on top of the route limit. When the shared ESI budget is nearly spent the call is refused with `503 upstream_busy` (MCP: an error result starting `upstream_busy`) and `Retry-After`; retry later.
- Arguments:
  - `system_name` (string): Solar system name, e.g. 'Tama' (single system; kills only)
  - `systems` (array of string): Up to 50 solar system names, e.g. ['1DQ1-A', 'Jita']: one line each, with jumps, ship kills, pod kills and NPC kills of the last hour
- Typed result (`result.data`): ActivityList with fields `systems`, `unresolved`
- Sources: EVE Static Data Export (via Fuzzwork); ESI (EVE Swagger Interface)

### find_systems

Find solar systems by filters and rank them: security band, region, constellation, faction, wormhole class, NPC station and its services, asteroid belts, planet types, ice belts (EVE University's list of highsec and lowsec ice systems) and distance from an origin (near). One line per system, up to 100 per call (page with offset), with the total. Example, the three nearest highsec Clear Icicle systems to C-N4OD: {"security":{"min":0.45},"ice_types":["Clear Icicle"],"near":{"origin":"C-N4OD"},"sort":"jumps","limit":3}. Set jump_range {origin, ship, jump_drive_calibration (default 5)} to keep the systems that ship can jump to from the origin (cyno-able: lowsec or nullsec, not wormhole space, Pochven or Zarzakh; 'Jump Bridge' = Ansiblex reach), with the light-years, sorted nearest first; e.g. the nearest lowsec NPC-station systems a Rorqual can reach from EC-P8R: {"jump_range":{"origin":"EC-P8R","ship":"Rorqual"},"security":{"min":0.1,"max":0.4},"has_npc_station":true,"limit":3}.

- Call: `POST /v1/tool/find_systems` or MCP tool `find_systems`
- Access: public. No key needed.
- Arguments:
  - `constellation` (string): Constellation name, e.g. 'Kimotoro'
  - `faction` (string): Faction name, e.g. 'Caldari State'
  - `has_ice_belt` (boolean): true for systems EVE University lists with ice belts, false for systems it does not list (nullsec ice systems are not covered)
  - `has_npc_station` (boolean): true for systems with an NPC station, false for systems without
  - `ice_types` (array of string): Ice types, e.g. ['Clear Icicle', 'Blue Ice']; a system matches when it has any of them; implies has_ice_belt
  - `jump_range` (object): Keep the systems a ship can jump to from an origin, with the light-years, nearest first, e.g. {"origin":"EC-P8R","ship":"Rorqual"}.
  - `limit` (integer): Systems per call (default 20, at most 100)
  - `min_asteroid_belts` (integer): At least this many asteroid belts, e.g. 3
  - `near` (object): Rank by gate jumps from an origin system and leave out systems with no gate route, e.g. {"origin":"C-N4OD","max_jumps":10}. Without max_jumps every reachable system is ranked.
  - `offset` (integer): Systems to skip, to read the next page (default 0)
  - `planet_types` (array of string): Planet types the system must have at least one of each, e.g. ['Lava', 'Gas']; an unknown name lists the valid ones
  - `region` (string): Region name, e.g. 'The Forge'
  - `security` (object): Security band as shown in game, e.g. 0.5 includes systems with true security 0.45-0.5: {"min":0.5} is highsec, {"max":0.4} is lowsec and below. Wormhole systems carry a security of about -1.0; filter them with wormhole_class (7, 8 and 9 are known-space highsec, lowsec and nullsec).
  - `sort` (string): Order: jumps (needs near; the default with near), security (most secure first), name (the default) or ly (needs jump_range; the default with jump_range). One of: jumps, security, name, ly.
  - `station_services` (array of string): Station services every match must offer, e.g. ['Reprocessing Plant', 'Factory']; an unknown name lists the valid ones
  - `wormhole_class` (integer): Wormhole class: 1-6 for C1-C6, 7 highsec, 8 lowsec, 9 nullsec, 12 Thera, 13 shattered frigate holes, 14-18 Drifter, 25 Pochven
- Typed result (`result.data`): SystemList with fields `total`, `offset`, `shown`, `sort`, `origin`, `systems`, `jump_range`
- Sources: EVE Static Data Export (via Fuzzwork); EVE University Wiki (ice belt systems)

### get_system_info

Facts about up to 50 solar systems in one call: security, region, constellation, faction, wormhole class and effect, neighbouring systems (stargates), counts of asteroid belts, moons, planets by type and NPC stations, and the ice belt when EVE University lists one. One line per system.

- Call: `POST /v1/tool/get_system_info` or MCP tool `get_system_info`
- Access: public. No key needed.
- Arguments:
  - `systems` (array of string, required): Up to 50 solar system names, e.g. ['Jita', 'Erkinen']: one line each
- Typed result (`result.data`): SystemInfoList with fields `systems`, `unresolved`, `not_enterable`
- Sources: EVE Static Data Export (via Fuzzwork); EVE University Wiki (ice belt systems)

### get_thera_connections

Live wormhole connections from Thera and Turnur into known space and wormhole space, from EvE-Scout (Signal Cartel's public scanning data; credit them as EvE-Scout / Signal Cartel). One line per connection: the exit system with its security and region, wormhole type and largest ship size, hours left and both signature ids. Set near {origin, max_jumps} to keep the exits closest to a system, sorted by jumps. Connections change every few hours.

- Call: `POST /v1/tool/get_thera_connections` or MCP tool `get_thera_connections`
- Access: public. No key needed.
- Live EvE-Scout data: Reads live Thera and Turnur connections from EvE-Scout (Signal Cartel) through a shared cache that follows its cache headers (one to ten minutes, five when they set none). When EvE-Scout does not answer, it serves its last copy if that is at most an hour old, with the copy's time in `as_of`; otherwise `result.text` says the connections are unavailable. All live-upstream calls share one fair-use limit of 5 calls per minute per caller without an API key and 10 with one (REST and MCP together, counted across every live tool), on top of the route limit.
- Arguments:
  - `hub` (string): Which hub's connections: 'thera', 'turnur' or 'all' (default). One of: thera, turnur, all.
  - `limit` (integer): Most connections to list (1-50, default 20); the answer says how many more there are
  - `near` (object): Keep the exits with a gate route to an origin system and sort them by jumps, e.g. {"origin":"Jita","max_jumps":10}. Exits with no gate route from the origin are left out (counted in the answer).
- Typed result (`result.data`): TheraConnections with fields `as_of`, `hub`, `origin`, `total`, `shown`, `left_out`, `connections`
- Sources: EvE-Scout / Signal Cartel; EVE Static Data Export (via Fuzzwork)

## MCP

- Hosted: streamable HTTP, stateless, JSON responses, at `/v1/mcp` on this host. One JSON-RPC message per request: batches are not accepted (`400 invalid_request`).
- Local: the `cmd/mcp` binary of this module speaks MCP over stdio (`go run ./cmd/mcp`), for Claude Desktop, Claude Code and other stdio hosts; it reads the SDE from `EVE_CORE_SDE_PATH`.
